summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package is a one-version 'Compatibility shim' under the @blueskydataplatform/* scope whose main entry (index.js) exports a Proxy of no-op functions and provides no advertised functionality. Its only runtime behavior is a beacon: beacon.cjs POSTs a JSON payload containing os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), and the Node version to the hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The beacon fires automatically from the postinstall lifecycle script (`node beacon.cjs`) on `npm install`, and again on any `require()`/`import` of the package via index.js calling `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()`. The shipped comment labels the behavior a 'build-provenance beacon', but the collected fields and hardcoded bare-IP destination are the canonical dependency-confusion reconnaissance shape against an internal npm scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
